{{MEinfobox
|name=Aggro
|cg=Aggro.png}}
{{StatusEffect|Aggro|r}} is a neutral effect that increases the chance of an Identity's skill slot being targeted by an enemy attack in focused encounters. 

==Summary==
{{StatusEffect|Aggro|r}} is an effect that is used by various units (such as Identities) to manipulate the probability of enemy Skills (which do not have properties such as {{SkillCon|Target Fixed}} and/or certain "Prioritizes targets with..." conditions) that target one of said affected Skill Slots. It is most common for Aggro to be used by Identities which are intended to fulfill the role of a tank. Aggro only influences gameplay in Focused Encounters, due to the fact that non-Focused Encounters do not allow for manual control over Skill targeting.


Aggro functions by changing the relative targeting weight (not to be confused with [[Slot weight|Slot Weight]]) of a unit's affected Skill Slots in respect to enemy Skills: as an example, on a group of units with 6 Skill Slots, any given Skill Slot of that group has a 1/6 chance of being the primary target of an enemy Skill; if something changes a Skill Slot's Aggro value to be above or below its default (in the case of Sinners this value is 500, which would be shown in-game as 5.00<ref>When under the effect of {{StatusEffect|Piercing Sword|b}}, a Sinner's visual Aggro value can range from 4.85 to as low as 4.25; thus, their default value is 5 (500 internally).</ref>; it is otherwise a value of 100, or 1.00 in game<ref>The decompiled function of SinManager.TargetManager.GetTargetSinActionModels_Using() specifies a partPoolUnit (_AGGRO_CORRECTION) value of 100, in the case of a target having more than 0 parts.</ref>), that Skill Slot's chance of being targeted by an enemy Skill linearly scales by its Aggro value. 


While in-game Aggro values can be reduced below a unit's default value (such as via the effect of {{StatusEffect|Piercing Sword|b}}), this is a simplification on the game's part for readability; internal Aggro values range from a minimum of 1 (shown in-game as 0.01) to around the game's signed 32-bit integer limit of ~2.147 billion (in-game: ~21.4 million).


Enemy Skills with [[Attack Weight]] and/or the {{StatusEffect|Unfocused Volley|r}} property only have '''their primary (solid-line: ⟶) target''' affected by Aggro; secondary (dashed-line: ⤑) targeting is unaffected. Outside of the Sinners, Aggro is used exclusively by the [[Peccatula#Invidiae|Peccatulum Invidiae]], although this has no effect on gameplay as the player can manually adjust targets.


{{StatusEffect|Aggro|r}} has other uses besides targeting manipulation: it can focus attacks upon units which are resistant to the damage type it is being targeted by, or allow for more attacks to be Evaded than what would otherwise be possible; it can enable unopposed attacks that would otherwise be impossible from units due to their Speed ranges; et cetera. Aggro's use can be more effective on smaller teams and/or against units with high amounts of Skill Slots.
